summary: The note contrasts the late 18th and early 19th century industrialisation of the UK and parts of Western Europe with the US, which was then mainly an agricultural and natural resource economy. It describes US transport building (roads, canals, steamboats, railroads) as a way of moving farm and resource goods across a large, sparsely populated country. It then states that the Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain, where many innovations originated, and attributes its causes partly to Britain's trading empire and the rise of business.
one_line: Overview of the Industrial Revolution's start in Britain and how the US, then an agricultural economy, developed transport infrastructure.
key_facts: During the late 18th and early 19th centuries, the UK and parts of Western Europe began to industrialise.
During the same period, the US was primarily an agricultural and natural resource producing and processing economy.
Roads and canals, steamboats, and railroads were important for handling agricultural and natural resource products in the large and sparsely populated US.
The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain.
Many of the technological innovations of the Industrial Revolution were British.
By the mid-18th century, Britain controlled a global trading empire with colonies in North America and Africa.
Britain had some political influence on the Indian subcontinent through the activities of the East India Company.
The development of trade and the rise of business were major causes of the Industrial Revolution.
